questions.q: Equal volumes of hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide of the same concentration are mixed. Which combined observation is most consistent with the source?
options: A) A nearly neutral pH is obtained and the temperature rises because neutralisation is exothermic
B) The solution remains strongly acidic and the temperature falls
C) The solution becomes strongly basic because NaOH always dominates HCl
D) No salt forms because equal volumes cancel the reaction
questions.answer: A) A nearly neutral pH is obtained and the temperature rises because neutralisation is exothermic
questions.explanation: Equal amounts of a strong acid and a strong base of the same concentration neutralise each other to form salt and water. The Exemplar source also states that acid-base mixing raises the temperature, showing that neutralisation is exothermic. Therefore a nearly neutral solution together with a temperature rise is the consistent outcome.

questions.q: A salt A used in bakery products gives, on heating, another salt B used for removing permanent hardness of water and a gas C that turns lime water milky. Which identification is correct?
options: A) A = washing soda, B = baking soda, C = H2
B) A = baking soda, B = sodium carbonate, C = CO2
C) A = common salt, B = bleaching powder, C = Cl2
D) A = gypsum, B = plaster of Paris, C = SO2
questions.answer: B) A = baking soda, B = sodium carbonate, C = CO2
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, a substance used in bakery products. On heating it forms sodium carbonate along with carbon dioxide and water; sodium carbonate is used in water-softening applications. Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky, so option B fits all three clues.

questions.q: In the chlor-alkali process, a gaseous by-product X reacts with lime to form a bleaching agent Y. Which pair correctly identifies X and Y?
options: A) X = H2, Y = washing soda
B) X = CO2, Y = baking soda
C) X = Cl2, Y = bleaching powder
D) X = O2, Y = plaster of Paris
questions.answer: C) X = Cl2, Y = bleaching powder
questions.explanation: Electrolysis of brine in the chlor-alkali process produces chlorine gas along with hydrogen and sodium hydroxide. The source states that chlorine reacts with lime to give the compound used as a bleaching agent. Thus X is chlorine and Y is bleaching powder.

questions.q: A white sulphate salt of a Group 2 element can be made into a mouldable paste, but after being left in the open it becomes a hard mass. Which explanation best matches this behaviour?
options: A) Washing soda loses all its sodium ions and becomes insoluble
B) Baking soda absorbs carbon dioxide and turns into common salt
C) Gypsum loses water and becomes calcium carbonate
D) Plaster of Paris takes up water and converts to gypsum, producing a hard solid mass
questions.answer: D) Plaster of Paris takes up water and converts to gypsum, producing a hard solid mass
questions.explanation: The mouldable material described is plaster of Paris, a partially hydrated calcium sulphate. When mixed with or exposed to water, it hydrates to gypsum. This hydration sets the material into a hard mass, which is why option D explains the observation.
